slides.title:
A tailor couldn't
afford *$68*. So he
wrote to Levi Strauss.
slides.sub:
How a few copper rivets
created blue jeans 👇

slides.title:
Gold Rush. Levi Strauss,
24, arrives in San Francisco
and sells *dry goods*.
slides.sub:
A German immigrant opening a West
Coast branch of his brothers' business
(Mental Floss, Levi Strauss & Co.).

slides.title:
A woman asks Reno tailor
Jacob Davis for pants
*made to be strong*.
slides.sub:
For her husband, who wore his
pants out fast (National Archives,
Mental Floss).

slides.title:
He adds *copper rivets*,
the ones he used on
horse blankets.
slides.sub:
At the pocket corners and the fly.
200+ pairs sold in 18 months
(Mental Floss, History.com).

slides.title:
The patent fee he
didn't have. So in 1872,
he *writes to Strauss*.
slides.sub:
You pay, we patent it together.
Strauss agrees enthusiastically
(Mental Floss, History.com).

slides.title: The employment of a metal rivet or eyelet at each edge of the pocket opening to *prevent the ripping* of the seam at those points.
slides.author:
Jacob W. Davis, U.S. patent No. 139,121
(1873, via the National Archives)

slides.title:
May 20: the patent is
granted. *Blue jeans*
are born.
slides.sub:
Davis moves to San Francisco to run
the factory for the rest of his life
(History.com, Levi's).

slides.title:
Levi Strauss & Co. net
revenues in fiscal 2025,
*up 4%*.
slides.sub:
Full-year results, January 28, 2026.
Direct-to-consumer: 49% of Q4
revenues (Levi Strauss & Co.).

slides.title:
Your next best seller
is in a *complaint*.
slides.sub:

his pants. Davis fixed it.
